newsitem.title: USA: Dutch cruise ship rescues Cuban refugee.
newsitem.headline: Dutch cruise ship rescues Cuban refugee.

text.p: A Cuban refugee who left the communist-ruled island in a makeshift boat fell into the lap of luxury on Friday when he was plucked from the Gulf of Mexico by the crew of a Dutch cruise ship.

The Holland America Line's Nieuw Amsterdam was sailing from Cozumel, Mexico, to New Orleans when passengers and crew spotted the rafter some 160 miles (260 km) northwest of Cuba, the company's public relations director, Larry Dessler, said.
The U.S. Coast Guard confirmed that the cruise line had radioed to say it was taking the refugee to New Orleans, where he would be turned over to the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service.
The rafter, Alex Hernandez Cruz, 29, from the Isle of Youth, said he had been at sea for 20 days, Dessler said.

"He starts off in a homemade wooden tub and ends his journey to freedom in a luxury cruise ship," Dessler said, adding that he was sailing in what the cruise line crew called "a wooden tub with a sail made of towels."
The ship's doctor said he was suffering from dehydration but was otherwise in good shape.
The U.S. Coast Guard frequently picks up Cuban refugees sailing makeshift vessels from the island to Florida. They are usually returned to Cuba.
